episode_title: He Played Ozzfest. Then He Got Into the Restaurant Business | Iano Dovi

real_qa.q: What bands did Yanni Dovey tour with before transitioning to the restaurant industry?
real_qa.r: Yanni Dovey toured with a band called Poison the Well for about a year, and later worked with main support bands at major festivals. He performed at Ozzfest and worked backstage with bands like Slipknot and Slayer, taking on roles including tour managing, lighting, guitar teching, drum teching, and front of house work over approximately seven to eight years.
real_qa.requete: Yanni Dovey Poison the Well Ozzfest touring

real_qa.q: How has The Attic maintained success over 14 years despite economic crises and industry changes?
real_qa.r: Yanni Dovey states that the through-line for The Attic's success has been his commitment to making it the last restaurant job his employees ever want to have, which requires him to be the best leader possible for them. He emphasizes creating an environment where team members feel comfortable, supported, and motivated to be better versions of themselves through respect, clarity, and individualized tools tailored to each person's needs.
real_qa.requete: The Attic Long Beach 14 years success restaurant leadership

real_qa.q: What is the Dovey Group's core mission and service offerings?
real_qa.r: The Dovey Group aims to tell stories and capture them for people who cannot speak to the world through film or audio, while also helping individual restaurant operators build and maintain cohesive teams. Yanni Dovey plans to deliver this through long-form and short-form content, live presentations, keynotes, and training workshops like Creating a Culture of Success, which teaches managers how to create environments where their teams can succeed.
real_qa.requete: Dovey Group hospitality media training storytelling

real_qa.q: How has technology transformed DJing since Yanni Dovey began in the 1990s?
real_qa.r: The biggest technological advancement for Yanni Dovey is being able to plug into Apple Music as a streaming service through Serato via Wi-Fi, eliminating the need to purchase and carry physical discs. This evolution went from lugging heavy record bags to now using compact equipment like Serato boxes or FaZe mixers; on his last DJ set, he simply logged into Apple Music and performed a 45-minute set without needles, USB, or a computer.
real_qa.requete: Serato Apple Music streaming DJ technology evolution

real_qa.q: What marketing strategies has Yanni Dovey applied from his music career to his current businesses?
real_qa.r: Yanni Dovey emphasizes getting the message out as much as possible, being excited about what you have, and putting real spirit and backbone behind your work. He shares that he is proud to listen to his own music, wear his own shirts, and talk about anything he is doing because that is his heart, soul, and spirit—and he believes people should share their authentic passion rather than viewing self-promotion as corny.
real_qa.requete: music marketing authentic self-promotion passion entrepreneurship

guest.bio_context: Yanni Dovey has worked in the restaurant industry for 14 years, starting as a server at The Attic in Long Beach before becoming General Manager. He also comes from an extensive music background spanning from the late 1990s to early 2000s, including touring as a musician with heavy metal bands, performing at Ozzfest, and working as a professional DJ with five residencies. He is now building the Dovey Group as a hospitality media company focused on leadership training and storytelling.
